vars.label: Land highly susceptible to landslides (USGS, %)
vars.ref: USGS landslide susceptibility map of Puerto Rico (Hughes and Schulz, 2020; Open-File Report 2020-1022; GIS layer, data release 10.5066/P990ZP4C), read from the first author's 5 m tile copy at zoom 15
vars.definition: The share of the land in the three highest classes of the USGS map of susceptibility to landslides triggered by intense rainfall (High, Very High and Extremely High: the most susceptible 30% of the main island). The USGS map ranks every 5 m cell of the main island by how likely it is to slide during or soon after intense rainfall, such as a hurricane's, and sorts the island into five classes by area: the 40% least susceptible is Low, then Moderate (30%), High (20%), Very High (9%) and Extremely High (the top 1%). The classes are relative to Puerto Rico, not a probability. It does not show where a slide travels downhill, and it is not a substitute for a site-specific slope-stability study. A barrio's share is the classified area of those classes over all its classified land, from the map read at about 4.5 m a pixel; a municipio's and Puerto Rico's shares come from the areas of their barrios. Vieques, Culebra and Isla de Mona are not in the map and have no value; Puerto Rico's figure is the main island's.
vars.noValue: Not mapped: the USGS susceptibility map covers the main island only

vars.label: Residents on land highly susceptible to landslides (estimate)
vars.ref: USGS landslide susceptibility map of Puerto Rico (Hughes and Schulz, 2020; Open-File Report 2020-1022; GIS layer, data release 10.5066/P990ZP4C), read from the first author's 5 m tile copy at zoom 15
vars.definition: The 2020 census residents living in the three highest classes of the USGS landslide susceptibility map (High, Very High and Extremely High). Each 2020 census block with residents counts whole in the class under its internal point (a block that a class edge crosses counts on one side), in the barrio that holds the point; the share is over all the 2020 residents of the area. An estimate, rough for a barrio. Vieques, Culebra and Isla de Mona have no value; Puerto Rico's figure is the main island's (the share is over the main island's 3,275,833 residents; the Economy tab's 'per 1,000 residents' view divides Puerto Rico's count by all 3,285,874 residents, Vieques and Culebra included, as it does for every dataset, so it reads 114.4 where the share reads 11.5%). A barrio with no residents in 2020 has no share.
